## Body

**Performance: PASS WITH NOTES** at `0eb43f285c5ede32ceccc232f7f23a6c150df23b`.

The PR contribution is the advertised four files, +408/-18, using the merge-base comparison. **`spawn_sites.rs` and the tmux launch producer are unchanged.** No new periodic loop, timer or launch site.

On the healthy live-control-client path, the close-note evaluation makes one `pane_process` IPC request for root PID/cwd, then process-start/liveness reads. When it obtains a root, it also fetches **the full registry**, including historical rows, and searches for another holder: O(S) decoding/matching plus the store's schema guard, even when the pane is judged Own. A missing recorded pane or failed/gone pane read returns earlier.

A non-self/non-parent close additionally checks the orphan exception: parented/live/unknown cases short-circuit; an observed-dead parentless candidate fetches **all projects** plus its schema guard and scans their designations, O(P). These costs are per explicit close, not per seat per tick. A memory-held close evaluates its initial note and evaluates again when the deferred close executes; it is not necessarily one read over the whole two-phase operation.

**P220-N001 / C34 qualification: “never a tmux launch” is not an unconditional property of this port.** `pane_process` uses `stdout -> control.query`, not `query_live`. The existing adapter may start/restart its persistent client and forks its recorded display-message fallback when the client is unavailable, disabled or times out. A failed pane read may also call `list_panes` to distinguish a missing pane. Liveness likewise retains its existing ps fallback for unanswered kernel reads. These are existing recorded producers newly exercised by this per-request check, not new launch sites or a new polling cadence. Normal live-client reads add no fork; the stronger unconditional zero-launch claim cannot be certified from this implementation. No measured normal-use cost breach established.
